label: Extreme Heat
summary: Heat is the deadliest weather hazard in New York City. Most heat deaths happen indoors, in homes without air conditioning. Risk is highest for older adults, people with chronic illness, and people living alone.

sections.title: Signs of heat illness
sections.body: Call 911 immediately for hot dry skin, confusion, fainting, or a temperature above 103°F. Heat exhaustion — heavy sweating, weakness, nausea, headache — can become heat stroke quickly. Move to a cool place and drink water.

sections.title: Staying safe indoors
sections.body: Use air conditioning if you have it, even briefly. A fan alone is not enough above about 95°F. Check on neighbours who live alone, are older, or have a chronic illness.
